data.title: Apple's retail footprint in India crosses 75,000 sq ft with Hyderabad entry
data.description:
Apple India has leased nearly 12,000 square feet (sq ft) of retail space at Lake Shore Mall in Hyderabad’s Kukatpally, bringing its retail footprint across seven stores in the country to 77,912 sq ft. The store, scheduled to open on December 10, will mark the American technology giant’s entry into Hyderabad.
 
According to property registration documents accessed by Propstack, a real estate data analytics firm, the technology giant signed a fresh lease for 10 years and nine months, starting April 15, 2026, with an option to renew for an additional five years.
 
Under the lease agreement, the technology giant is leasing space on the lower ground and ground floors of the Hyderabad mall.
  
The deal terms include a monthly rent of ₹18.5 lakh for an area spanning 11,890 sq ft. The rent will be paid quarterly at ₹55.51 lakh, translating to a rate of ₹155.50 per sq ft per month.
 
Apple Kukatpally will join the company’s growing network of stores in India, including Apple BKC and Apple Borivali in Mumbai, Apple Saket and Apple Noida in Delhi-NCR, Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru, and Apple Koregaon Park in Pune.
 
Before the Hyderabad addition, Apple’s latest store opened in February 2026 at Oberoi Sky City Mall in Mumbai’s Borivali, spanning 12,616 sq ft. That store was the company’s sixth in India and second in Mumbai.
 
With the addition of the Hyderabad store, Apple’s retail footprint across these seven malls in India will reach 77,912 sq ft. This includes 7,997 sq ft at Phoenix Mall of Asia in Bengaluru, 20,806 sq ft at Jio World Drive in Mumbai, 8,418 sq ft at Select Citywalk in Delhi, 8,240 sq ft at DLF Mall of India in Noida, and 7,945 sq ft at The Kopa in Pune.
 
The store’s barricade, unveiled ahead of the opening, features a pearl-inspired Apple logo against iridescent tones, drawing on Hyderabad’s identity as the ‘City of Pearls’ and its centuries-old tradition of pearl processing and refining.
 
The city, a leading centre for technology and entrepreneurship, also houses Apple’s research and development and retail customer care teams. Apple has been looking to expand its presence in India, which the company has described as a market with significant growth potential.

data.title: RBI urges banks to expedite MSME lending, reduce reliance on collateral
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has urged banks to expedite credit sanctions to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and reduce their reliance on collateral, encouraging cash-flow-based lending through digital channels to improve access to finance for the sector.
 
At the 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) on MSME credit in Kolkata, Deputy Governor Swaminathan J called for greater use of the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and other digital channels to facilitate lending to MSMEs, the RBI said in a press release.
 
He also emphasised the need to expand the use of the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) for receivables financing and strengthen early identification and resolution of stress among MSME borrowers.
 
 
The meeting reviewed the flow of working capital and investment credit to MSMEs, lending to first-time borrowers, and credit guarantee coverage. Discussions also covered the enhanced limit for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of invoices of central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) through TReDS, and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.
 
Recognising the contribution of MSMEs to India's economic growth and development goals, the deputy governor also called on industry associations to actively participate in the RBI's outreach initiatives, including town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings.
 
Such engagements would help improve awareness of credit-related initiatives and enable industry associations to raise concerns of their members with banks, according to the RBI.
 
The meeting was attended by representatives of the Ministry of MSME, the Department of Financial Services, select banks, Sidbi, Nabard, CGTMSE, NCGTC, KVIC, the Indian Banks' Association, and national, regional, and state-level MSME associations.

data.title: 136 vessels of Indian interest impacted in troubled waters since March
data.description:
Wars and piracy in global waters have affected 136 vessels of Indian interests in the past eight months, leading to the deaths of 16 Indian seafarers while five remain missing and 34 have been injured, a Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) report has said.
 
The DGMA’s latest security report covers attacks and other incidents on three major routes between March 1 and November 1. The routes are the Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman, the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Bab-el-Mandeb, and the Black Sea.
 
The Strait of Hormuz/Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman region accounted for 93 affected vessels, including six Indian-flagged and 87 foreign-flagged vessels, with 11 fatalities, three missing crew members, and 27 injuries reported.
 
 
In the Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Bab-el-Mandeb region, six vessels were affected while the Black Sea recorded incidents involving 37 foreign-flagged vessels, resulting in five fatalities, two missing crew members, and six injuries.
 
Overall, the data highlights the significant impact of geopolitical tensions and maritime security threats on commercial shipping and the safety of Indian and foreign seafarers, the DGMA said.
 
11 seafarers still under captivity
The DGMA report also shows that 11 Indian seafarers who were aboard a vessel captured by pirates are still held captive along with 11 foreign seafarers. These seafarers were aboard the MT Asana, which was captured on July 17.
 
The data shows that 46 Indian seafarers have so far been impacted by piracy in the last eight months.
 
Seven incidents related to piracy, hijacking and armed robbery involving vessels with Indian crew members are reflected in the data, the DGMA said.
 
The remaining vessels, except the MT Asana, have been released, have resumed their voyages, or have reported the safe release of their crew, the maritime regulator’s report said.
 
Attacks in war-stricken waters have become a major concern for the government and maritime stakeholders, and seafarer unions have called for a stop to the targeting of commercial vessels.

data.title: Credai seeks affordable housing reforms, tax relief ahead of FY28 Budget
data.description:
The Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (Credai), an industry body representing private real estate developers, has sought reforms to align the definition of affordable housing with current market conditions and improve affordability for homebuyers, among its several suggestions to the finance ministry ahead of the Union Budget 2027-28.
 
Credai said in a statement on Friday that it had also sought enhanced access to housing finance through tax benefits and a reduction in long-term capital gains tax on land and buildings to support sustained investment in the sector, adding that it had shared these recommendations with the ministry during the pre-Budget consultations with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on November 20.
 
 
The recommendations come against the backdrop of a continued decline in the supply of affordable housing. The share of homes priced below ₹50 lakh across the top eight cities fell from 54 per cent in 2018 to 21 per cent in 2025, the statement showed. This decline reflects the growing affordability challenge amid rising land and construction costs, it added.
 
Separately, data from real estate consultancy Anarock showed that the share of housing supply priced below ₹40 lakh declined from 26 per cent to 10 per cent during the first nine months of 2026.
 
Credai President Shekar Patel said the body's demands for reforms in affordable housing came amid India's expanding housing requirements due to urbanisation and continued strong demand for affordable housing.
 
“There is a need to revisit the existing affordable housing definition to align it with evolving market realities. Tax thresholds need to reflect current property and construction costs,” Patel added.
 
The body has proposed a uniform, area-based definition of affordable housing across goods and services tax (GST), income tax, and priority sector lending. It has recommended limits based on Rera carpet area of 70 square metres (sq m) in notified metros, 90 sq m in urban centres with a population of 10 lakh and above, and 120 sq m elsewhere.
 
If a price ceiling is required for income tax purposes, Credai has recommended raising it to ₹90 lakh, with an annual escalation of 5 per cent to account for inflation and rising raw material and labour costs, the statement said.
 
To improve project viability, the association has sought the reintroduction of the incentive under the former Section 80-IBA through a new Section 142A. The proposal provides for a 100 per cent deduction on profits from eligible projects approved between April 2027 and March 2032. It also seeks to extend the benefit to companies, firms, and limited liability partnerships (LLPs), with exemptions from minimum alternate tax (MAT) and alternate minimum tax (AMT).
 
For homebuyers, Credai has recommended enhancing the tax deduction on housing loan interest for first-time homebuyers under the proposed affordable housing definition. The association has also proposed extending this benefit under both the old and new income tax regimes to improve affordability and encourage homeownership.
 
Further, to expand access to formal housing finance, Credai has proposed strengthening the credit guarantee mechanism for affordable home loans. This includes revising and increasing the existing loan ceiling of ₹20 lakh in line with prevailing market conditions and property rates, with a uniform 75 per cent guarantee cover. Eligibility should be linked to the value of the house rather than the borrower's income category, it said.
 
Credai has also proposed a 10-year income tax exemption on rental income from eligible affordable homes, subject to specified conditions relating to tenancy and vacancy. The measure is aimed at encouraging investment in formal rental housing and increasing the availability of affordable homes in urban centres.
 
A key recommendation is to reduce long-term capital gains tax on land and buildings held for two years or more to 5 per cent, applicable to all taxpayers, including non-residents. The proposal is intended to lower the tax burden on land transactions and encourage landowners to bring land into the development market, particularly through joint development arrangements.
 
The association has also proposed a uniform 5 per cent tax rate on other long-term capital gains and dividend income, subject to specified holding periods and tax provisions. For businesses, it has sought an optional 22 per cent tax regime for partnership firms and LLPs that forgo exemptions, bringing their tax treatment closer to that available to companies.
 
Credai has also recommended a 15 per cent tax rate for new service-sector units established in special economic zones (SEZs) between April 2027 and March 2031, with the benefit available for 10 years. The proposal is aimed at improving the competitiveness of SEZs in attracting new service-sector investment.
 
“Our recommendations seek to address these constraints through targeted fiscal measures that can improve affordability for buyers, make projects viable and encourage the release of land for development. A more consistent tax framework for housing will also support employment, investment and planned urban growth,” Patel said.

data.title: Small- and mid-cap funds retain folio lead despite sharp October slowdown
data.description:
Small- and mid-cap (SMID) funds continued to account for the bulk of folio additions in the active equity category in October, even as the pace of new additions nearly halved from the previous month amid a correction in the broader market.
 
The two categories together accounted for 56.9 per cent of active equity folio additions in October, marginally lower than 57.9 per cent in September. This was despite the combined additions declining 47.4 per cent to 539,000 from 1 million a month earlier.
 
The net inflows into the two categories also plunged last month. They garnered net inflows of ₹11,300 crore in October, down 33 per cent from the all-time high of ₹16,873 crore in September. The decline in folio growth as well as net inflows came as the broader market corrected for the second consecutive month in October. The Nifty Smallcap 250 declined almost 6 per cent, while the Nifty Midcap 150 slipped almost 4 per cent last month. In comparison, the Nifty 50 gained about 2 per cent.
 
 
The data highlights that small- and mid-cap funds remain key to mutual fund (MF) folio growth. Experts say that the higher investor interest in the two categories stems from expectations of better performance, and the trend can reverse only if large-caps deliver sustained outperformance.
 
"We see two likely reasons for the strong share of new folios in small- and mid-cap funds. The first is the expectation of faster earnings growth. Investors see room for smaller businesses to expand into new markets and gain market share as they grow. The second factor is relative performance. Over the past year, small- and mid-cap funds have generally compared favourably with large-cap funds," said Sorbh Gupta, head of equities, Bajaj Asset Management.
 
"If large-cap funds sustain a period of stronger relative performance, they could begin to attract a higher share of new folios," he added.
 
The outperformance of small- and mid-caps in the past three-four years has resulted in sharp growth in folios as well as the assets under management (AUM) of schemes focusing on these segments.
 
Within the equity category, small-cap and sectoral/thematic funds recorded the fastest growth over the seven-year period between October 2019 and October 2026. Small-cap AUM expanded 9.2 times at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 37.3 per cent, while sectoral/thematic funds grew 8.3 times at a CAGR of 35.3 per cent. Large- and mid-cap funds and mid-cap funds also recorded strong CAGRs of 30.2 per cent and 29.6 per cent, respectively, ICRA Analytics stated in its recent report.

data.title: Trai extends 1601 numbering series to consumer-facing sectors in Phase 2
data.description:
India’s telecom regulator on Friday extended the use of the 1601 numbering series to consumer-facing services, including retail chains, e-commerce, commercial airlines, ride-hailing and food aggregator apps, travel agencies, and telecom service providers, among others.
 
In its directions, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) said the 1601 series would be available for service and transactional voice calls to these additional sectors under the second phase, which will help consumers identify legitimate calls and prevent fraud and impersonation.
 
“Being a trusted channel, the numbers from this series are allocated only to the verified entities, and thereby helping consumers to easily identify legitimate service and transactional calls. This measure is an important tool in combating impersonation by fraudsters who use normal 10-digit numbers and falsely claim to represent legitimate businesses,” Trai said.
  
In the first phase that began in August this year, the 1601 series was made available to electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution companies, LPG distributors, and other utility service providers. Courier, express logistics, parcel delivery, freight, and logistics companies engaged in delivering consignments were also eligible for the series.
 
Trai had earlier mandated the use of the 1600 series for service and transaction-related calls by banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) entities and for government-to-citizen communication. The series was introduced in January 2026. Entities cannot make promotional calls from the numbering series.
 
In the second phase, Trai said that the 1601 series would be used by retail chains, e-commerce companies, hospitals, diagnostic laboratories, telecom service providers, internet service providers, automobile sales, repair and servicing businesses, travel agencies, commercial airlines, food aggregators, ride-hailing aggregators, and lending service providers. “Only the entities having an annual turnover of ₹500 crore or more in at least one of the preceding three financial years shall be eligible,” the regulator specified.
 
Distribution platform operators such as direct-to-home, headend-in-the-sky, internet protocol television (IPTV) service providers, and multi-system operators having a subscriber base of 1 million or more in any month during the preceding 12 months would also be eligible.
 
“The 1601-series numbers shall be assigned only to the companies registered in India under the applicable law,” the regulator added.
 
Telcos have been directed to complete the onboarding and migration of all eligible entities within 180 days, and they will have to publicise the availability of the series among eligible entities, submit status reports to Trai every 15 days, and submit a final compliance report after 6.5 months. “Based on a review of the implementation, the Authority may notify additional sectors or eligible entities from time to time,” the regulator added.

data.title: Niti Aayog weighs measures to reduce import dependence in capital goods
data.description:
Amid the growing practice of countries imposing trade curbs on critical components, Niti Aayog is assessing India’s current import dependence in the capital goods market and finalising policy recommendations on both reducing India’s dependence on imports and raising its share in the global supply chain.
 
According to people familiar with the matter, the recommendations could largely be regulatory and institutional, and officials have sought inputs on possible bottlenecks that can be eased to enable more domestic manufacturing of capital goods.
 
“There are two types of dependence. One, where there is complete dependence on other countries for capital goods, and another where a large majority of the manufacturing happens here but crucial components come from countries like China, which know exactly where each critical component they are exporting stands in the global supply chain, and use export controls as leverage. Niti is looking at both these aspects,” an official said.
 
 
The move comes amid increasing calls from the government to increase self-reliance and manufacturing. At the Ficci annual general meeting, Prime Minister Narendra Modi identified hand tools, power tools, and machinery manufacturing – all capital goods – as areas with significant export potential, particularly in developing countries and the Global South.
 
Niti Aayog is likely to prepare a report as part of its trade assessment exercise. Queries sent to Niti Aayog remained unanswered at the time of publication.
 
The move also assumes significance in the wake of recent curbs announced by China on critical construction equipment such as tunnel boring machines (TBMs), which are required by India for major tunnel infrastructure projects across highways, railways, metro rail, and energy.
 
The Cabinet on Wednesday announced an ₹11,000 crore scheme to support the manufacturing of heavy construction equipment to tackle these issues and build an ecosystem in India for what is an important part of the capital goods segment.
 
While it has sought inputs from stakeholders in the sector, the think tank is learnt to be not too keen on financial sops such as tax breaks and manufacturing assistance subsidy programmes. Niti Aayog would look at ways to encourage research and development (R&D), which remains a key area of concern not just in capital goods but across sectors.
 
The Ministry of Heavy Industries has been running the National Capital Goods Policy for a decade, and the second phase of the programme is under way. Under the ₹1,207 crore Phase II, 29 projects have been sanctioned, including centres of excellence, common engineering facilities, testing and certification centres, and technology accelerators.
 
The FY27 Budget also proposed two hi-tech tool rooms to support local design, testing, and production of high-precision components.
 
In a report last week, the Confederation of Indian Industry and Boston Consulting Group recommended a focus on capital goods in emerging sectors such as semiconductors and data centres. Potential approaches include extending selected incentive benefits (e.g., the Semicon India Programme) to domestic capital goods development and procurement, with phased, product-specific domestic value addition (DVA) thresholds verified through factory audits.
 
“Government could also review duty inversions where, for instance, finished equipment used in electronics manufacturing attracts lower duty than inputs and sub-assemblies needed to make it domestically. Any resulting structural cost disadvantage for domestic manufacturers could be addressed by aligning duties on identified inputs,” the report said.
 
It also recommended incentives for R&D and closing the financing gap between Indian players and their global peers.
 
According to the report, India has an import dependence of 38 per cent or more in seven of the 10 subsectors in capital goods, while three subsectors – plastic processing, machine tools, and textile machinery – have import dependence of between 59 and 67 per cent.

data.title: HC quashes appointment of rebel TMC camp's Ritabrata Banerjee as LoP
data.description:
The Calcutta High Court on Friday set aside the appointment of rebel TMC faction's Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly, holding that it was not sustainable under law.

The court also quashed the appointment of Akhruzzaman as Chief Whip of the TMC.

Justice Krishna Rao directed Speaker Rathindra Bose to consider afresh the appointment of the LoP and the Chief Whip within 10 days.

In a judgment on a petition by TMC leader Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay challenging the appointments, the court held that the decision to appoint Banerjee as the LoP and Akhruzzaman as the Chief Whip was not sustainable under law.

 

Bose had appointed Banerjee as the Leader of Opposition on June 3 after the BJP was voted to power in May.

data.title: OTT releases this week: Hanuman Ansh, Spider-Man and more to watch online
data.description:
The final week of November brings a mix of Bollywood thrillers, Hollywood superhero films, science-fiction dramas and Korean romantic series to OTT platforms. From the much-awaited spiritual biopic, Hanuman Ansh, among the key Indian releases, Spider-Man: Brand New Day adds superhero shows to the lineup. 
 
Several OTT platforms featured in this week's streaming schedule arriving in the last week of November 2026 are returning with new stories, along with a few interesting titles for viewers who enjoy multiple genres.

Top 5 OTT releases to watch online this week

Hanuman Ansh
 
Release Date: November 27/November 29
 
Platform: SonyLIV, Netflix
 
Hanuman Ansh is a Hindi spiritual drama drawn from the experiences and lessons of the popular Neem Karoli Baba, commonly referred to as Maharaj-ji. Under the direction of Vishal Chaturvedi, the movie tells the story of a young boy who sets off on a spiritual journey that ultimately guides him to embrace a life filled with belief, kindness, and selfless service.
 
 
Spider-Man: Brand New Day
 
Reported Release Date: November 26
 
Platform: Netflix
 
Spider-Man: Brand New Day centers on Peter Parker as he adjusts to life in New York after the happenings of Spider-Man: No Way Home. Tom Holland reprises his role as the iconic web-slinger who confronts fresh dangers while managing the repercussions of his changed situation. 
 
This film blends superhero action with Peter's individual hardships. The cast includes Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Sink, Mark Ruffalo, and Jon Bernthal, among others. 
 
Drishyam: The Conclusion
 
Release Date: November 27 
Platform: Netflix
 
Ajay Devgn reprises his role as Vijay Salgaonkar in Drishyam: The Conclusion, the latest installment of the Hindi crime-thriller series. Under the direction of Abhishek Pathak, the story continues Vijay's ongoing struggle to protect his family and keep their secrets sealed. 
 
A new inquiry spearheaded by SP Rajveer Singh Tomar, portrayed by Jaideep Ahlawat, places additional strain on the Salgaonkar family. The cast also includes Tabu, Shriya Saran, Rajat Kapoor, Prakash Raj, Ishita Dutta, and Mrunal Jadhav.
 
Supergirl
 
Reported Release Date: November 26
 
Platform: JioHotstar
 
DC's Supergirl centers around Kara Zor-El, portrayed by Milly Alcock, as she transforms her personal loss into a broader battle for justice. While traveling on her birthday, Kara meets a girl named Ruthye, who has just lost her father to a ruthless outlaw. 
 
After Kara’s dog Krypto is poisoned, she partners with Ruthye to seek vengeance and find a cure. Directed by Craig Gillespie, the film features performances from Eve Ridley and Matthias Schoenaerts.
 
Delhi 2021
 
Release Date: November 25
 
Platform: ZEE5
 
Delhi 2021 is a film that unfolds during the devastating second wave of the COVID-19 outbreak in the capital city of India. The narrative centers on Manjot, portrayed by Richa Chadha, who is a nurse at SL Criticare Hospital as the city battles a lack of hospital beds and medical oxygen supplies. 
 
As the strain on healthcare professionals escalates, she battles to rescue her patients while facing the emotional and professional impacts of the ongoing emergency.

data.title: IndiGo stock gains altitude; oil, geopolitics and rupee remain key risks
data.description:
The aviation sector saw some relief in November due to moderation in fuel prices and a strengthening rupee. The strengthening of the rupee has reduced the cost of dollar-denominated lease rentals and also reverses mark-to-market (MTM) losses. Fuel costs account for roughly 40 per cent of operating costs, so this may mean a sequential margin rebound. The dominant domestic player, IndiGo (InterGlobe Aviation), would be the biggest gainer.
 
Brent crude and Singapore jet fuel prices have eased. Brent is down 22 per cent to $92 per barrel in November 2026 versus $104 in October. Singapore jet fuel is at $142 per barrel, down 16 per cent. The rupee is now at 93.3 per dollar, up from 96.9 in October. But crude is up 46 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y), jet fuel is up 59 per cent Y-o-Y, and the rupee is down 4 per cent Y-o-Y. So, while the sequential improvement is substantial, costs are well above levels seen in the October-December quarter (Q3) of FY26.
 
IndiGo posted standalone earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) of ₹3,160 crore in the July-September quarter (Q2) of FY27. Available seat kilometres (ASK) fell 1 per cent Y-o-Y, while the passenger load factor (PLF) was flat at 80.3 per cent. Total revenue was ₹23,400 crore, up 26 per cent Y-o-Y. Fuel expenses were down 8 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) as IndiGo responded to high costs with capacity and network adjustments and fare hikes. The reported net loss in Q2FY27 was ₹2,060 crore, with other income down 10 per cent Y-o-Y at ₹940 crore and MTM forex losses of ₹1,370 crore.
 
In October 2026, IndiGo and Akasa Air gained domestic market share, holding 66.1 per cent (up 61 basis points, or bps, Y-o-Y) and 6.7 per cent (up 154 bps Y-o-Y), respectively, at the expense of Air India Group and SpiceJet. Air India’s market share declined 109 bps to 24.7 per cent, and SpiceJet’s market share declined 152 bps Y-o-Y to 1 per cent. On international routes, IndiGo’s market share rose to 48.8 per cent (up 154 bps Y-o-Y) at the expense of SpiceJet, whose market share fell 154 bps Y-o-Y to 2 per cent, while the market shares of Air India Group and Akasa Air were stable at 46.5 per cent and 2.7 per cent, respectively.
 
This was a difficult market with high costs and subdued traffic. Domestic airlines carried 13.3 million passengers in October 2026, down 5 per cent Y-o-Y, with revenue passenger kilometres (RPK) down 5 per cent Y-o-Y. Flight departures were down 6 per cent Y-o-Y, and ASK was down 3 per cent Y-o-Y, as airlines prioritised yields and margin protection over growth. Traffic demand was subdued, and PLF declined 74 bps month-on-month (M-o-M) to 80.4 per cent.
 
The November M-o-M data for ASK, RPK, PLF, etc., will be key monitorables. IndiGo’s guidance is that ASK for Q3FY27 will see low single-digit growth Y-o-Y. Passenger revenue per ASK (PRASK) should rise by more than 25 per cent Y-o-Y. The PLF would be flat. ASK for FY27 will see low single-digit growth.
 
In international traffic, a sequential recovery was visible in October over September. International passenger traffic carried by Indian airlines declined 13 per cent Y-o-Y to 2.6 million in October 2026, with departures down 11 per cent Y-o-Y. RPK declined 12 per cent Y-o-Y, and PLF fell 287 bps Y-o-Y to 75.4 per cent. But there was a 500 bps M-o-M improvement in PLF and a 4 per cent M-o-M rise in passengers. Sustaining the sequential recovery will depend on easing geopolitical tensions and further moderation in operating costs.
 
In FY27 so far, domestic passenger traffic was down 2 per cent, with RPK also down 2 per cent Y-o-Y, and departures fell 4 per cent. In international traffic, Indian carriers’ passenger numbers were down 18 per cent, and RPK was down 13 per cent. Airlines have focused on yields, cash flow generation, and margin protection over volume growth, given high costs.
 
IndiGo has grown revenue steadily, but margins have been hit by surging aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices and forex losses on an MTM basis. It holds a dominant market share, with free cash of ₹39,900 crore on the balance sheet, and it will be writing off accumulated tax losses until FY28. IndiGo’s order book stands at 900 aircraft. Air India has 513 aircraft on order, while Akasa has 196 on order and SpiceJet has 120.
 
IndiGo has indicated that it will add one aircraft per week to the fleet until FY30. Assuming 50 new aircraft every year, ASK would grow by 10 per cent annually between FY26 and FY29. If PLF stays at 85 per cent, RPK (an indicator of utilisation) will grow at a similar rate to ASK. If the EBITDA margin is stable in the range of 25-27 per cent, EBITDA should rise 15-16 per cent annually during FY26-FY29.
 
This remains a weak environment, with geopolitical tensions and crude prices directly linked to conflicts. Delays in aircraft deliveries are another risk. But IndiGo will be well placed as and when tensions ease and the cycle changes.
 
The stock is up over 22 per cent in the past month and closed at ₹5,655 on Friday on the BSE. According to Bloomberg, all seven analysts polled in November (including three this week) are bullish on the stock, and their average one-year target price is ₹6,235.
